_about: Engine manifest: one entry per registered engine command (status planned, no code yet), per gate the engine runs (status on, card MW-003, with on_failure_reason: one line per gate) and per written but unregistered gate (status off-today). A gate in two groups has two entries on one function (MW-003 decision 1). Replaced by MW-003: rule_lock, card_test_lock, rule_code_lock, process_lock and discussion_freeze by lock, subtask_gate by subtask; the lock_notice entries are deleted, lock_notice joins the start line (D-1). Product checks are not here; they come from the branch profile's product_checks[]. name is unique; gate is the profile switch (gates.<gate>.on). group is the dispatcher group: one hook entry per event and group, `mkway/engine/mkway.py hook <event> --group <group>` (decision C10: start, edit, shell, post, prompt, stop). function is the gate's module:function, null until the gate is written (card MW-003); reason_ids lists the reason ids the gate may return, and a gate with none is not loaded. matcher null = no matcher (every tool); the dispatcher filters each gate by its own matcher. An entry's onFailure is applied by the dispatcher per gate (block = refuse gate-error; anything else = allow); 'none' is the source's word for no blocking. groups is the group table, an engine constant (R13c): the hook entry of a group carries the group's onFailure (edit and shell: block, so a timeout or crash of the dispatcher blocks the tool call); turning a gate on never changes it. class (MW-012) is integrity or form; a missing class reads integrity. An integrity gate never degrades and never reads a watch marker; a form gate may go into watch mode (see engine/gatemode.py). Order of the shell group (R281a, MW-110): Gates that decide WHO acts (lead.shell, message.session) run before lock.shell, the gate that decides WHAT may be touched and writes the permit, so a command refused for who acts leaves no permit. A chained or piped command that holds a state-changing engine call (send among them) is refused by lock.shell as not plain before any permit is written. Known gap (R281 point 7): a gate after lock.shell that refused a plain send command would leave its permit behind; no gate does today; the cure is the dispatcher applying effects only when nothing refused.

entries.name: lead.edit
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a registered lead write a file it may not; the gate allows a session it cannot prove is a lead, so a crash blocks only that call; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: lead.shell
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a registered lead write a file it may not or take a card; the owner's way out is their own terminal, where no hook runs

entries.name: message.session
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a session pass as another session, so a crash blocks that call; the identity a gate relies on is wiring and never watches; the owner's way out is their own terminal, where no hook runs

entries.name: lock.edit
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a write into a closed target through; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: outside.edit
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a write outside the session's root through; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: subtask
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let an edit outside the session's open card through; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: owner_ask.edit
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let an ask be written with no sources behind it; the gate allows a path it cannot prove is an ask path, so a crash blocks only the one edit; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: search
entries.on_failure_reason: a question is not worth blocking on a failure of the gate's own reading: it fails open (an error is a gate-error row, an unreadable transcript is the log row search-unverified); the owner sees the rows on the start line counts

entries.name: outbox_check.pre
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a check of the wrong text through; the gate allows a path it cannot prove is a check path, so a crash blocks only the one write; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: lock.shell
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a write into a closed target through; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: outside.shell
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a write outside the session's root through; the owner's way out is their own terminal

entries.name: commit_files
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a commit of the wrong files through; the owner's way out is their own terminal, where no hook runs

entries.name: delete
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a delete through that was not backed up; the owner's way out is their own terminal, where no hook runs

entries.name: commit_tests
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a commit through that was never tested; the owner's way out is their own terminal, where no hook runs

entries.name: message.send
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not cut a session off from its lead, so the gate fails open (a gate-error row); the inbox row stays the record and the start block and the prompt still list what is unacked; the owner's way out is `mkway gate watch message`

entries.name: records
entries.on_failure_reason: the tool already ran, so a block undoes nothing; a failed record is a refusal (post-record-failed, R271c-D1) that names the path, so the session does not go on believing it recorded; the next gate's refusal is the second signal

entries.name: agent_start
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash of the hook must not block the agent; a failed write refuses the start and names the path (agent-record-failed, R271c-D1)

entries.name: agent_stop
entries.on_failure_reason: a block here would keep a finished agent going; a failed write is a visible message that names the path (agent-record-failed, R271c-D1), never a refusal

entries.name: owner_ask.notify
entries.on_failure_reason: the write already happened, so a block undoes nothing; a failed owner record is a refusal (ask-record-failed, R271c-D1) that names the path; a failed notification is a log row (notify-failed), and the board still lists the ask

entries.name: outbox_check.post
entries.on_failure_reason: the write already happened, so a block undoes nothing; a failed record is a refusal (check-record-failed, R271c-D1) that names the path, and the check reads unproven until it is written again

entries.name: lead.remind
entries.on_failure_reason: a reminder only: a failure must not block the prompt; the notices stay in the lead's inbox and `mkway leads` lists them

entries.name: unresolved
entries.on_failure_reason: a reminder only: a failure must not block the prompt; the log row stays and the start line counts it

entries.name: owner_ask.remind
entries.on_failure_reason: a reminder only: a failure must not block the prompt; the board still shows the ask

entries.name: message.remind
entries.on_failure_reason: a reminder only: a failure must not block the prompt; the rows stay in the inbox and `mkway board` lists them

entries.name: owner_ask.stop
entries.on_failure_reason: named limit (K8): onFailure has no effect on a Stop hook, so a crashing Stop hook cannot block, and Claude Code ends the turn after eight blocks in a row; the gate allows on a crash with a calls-log error row and a start-line notice, and an ask file is still gated by the edit gate

entries.name: message.stop
entries.on_failure_reason: a Stop gate that fails must not trap the session in its reply; it is a reminder line and never a block, and the order stays listed in the inbox

entries.name: own_files_stop
entries.note: platform store, undocumented: reads the user's home folder; optional, fails open; on only when the branch profile turns it on

entries.name: tests.shape
entries.on_failure_reason: a crash must not let a commit of badly shaped tests through; the gate itself allows a commit it cannot read, so a crash blocks only that call; the owner's way out is `tests.shape.mode` watch in the profile, or their own terminal, where no hook runs

entries.name: outbox_check.stop
entries.on_failure_reason: a reminder only: a Stop gate that fails must not trap the session; it allows, and the write gate and the card close still judge the check

entries.name: ping.stop
entries.on_failure_reason: a Stop gate that fails must not trap the session in its reply; it allows, and the inbox row stays the record: the lead's start block and prompt still list what is unacked; the owner's way out is gates.ping.mode watch

entries.name: reader_allowlist
entries.on_failure_reason: MW-116 (R287c): the hook lives in the reader agent's own frontmatter (frontmatter: true), runs only inside the reader subagent after the workspace trust dialog, and is no settings entry; it blocks itself with exit 2 on every crash; its fail-closed proof is the record row of each call, not onFailure: a verdict for a run with no row is refused verdict-reader-unguarded

entries.name: inbox_waiter
entries.on_failure_reason: the waiter is no gate and never refuses: its own Stop handler (asyncRewake) wakes an idle lead or card holder when a new row reaches its inbox, and a crash of it exits 0, so a Stop is never blocked; the hook timeout is wake.deadline_seconds plus 60 (MW-078)
